title: Attorney General of Arizona

context.text: Mayes was elected in 2022 by 280 votes; Petersen won the July 21, 2026 Republican primary with 55.9% over Rodney Glassman, and Mayes was unopposed in the Democratic primary.

candidates.name: Kris Mayes
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Prosecuting drug smugglers, fraudsters and scammers; her survey says her office has seized 27 million fentanyl pills.
Consumer protection, including suits against RealPage and landlords over rent pricing, and opposing utility rate increases.
Protecting election systems, voter privacy and access to reproductive care.

record.text: Announced a lawsuit against OpenAI on October 14, 2026 alleging violations of the Arizona Consumer Fraud Act over the marketing and design of ChatGPT as it affects minors.
Filed a consumer-protection lawsuit against TikTok on October 8, 2026 alleging violations of the Arizona Consumer Fraud Act over features aimed at minors.
Urged the Arizona Corporation Commission on October 9, 2026 to investigate whether an APS adjuster shifted nearly $600 million in costs from large energy users to other customers.
Joined a multistate comment letter on October 7, 2026 opposing an HHS proposal to cut Head Start program standards.

statements.quote: She fought to protect access to reproductive care
statements.context: From her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response.

statements.quote: Her record is 2-0 for Arizona at the U.S Supreme Court, overturning illegal tariffs costing Arizonans an average $1,500 a year
statements.context: From her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response.

candidates.name: Warren Petersen
candidates.currentRole: President of the Arizona Senate; state senator, District 14

priorities.text: Fighting crime: prosecuting violent offenders, drug cartels and human trafficking.
Prosecuting government and consumer fraud and reviewing state contracts and regulatory decisions.
Enforcing state statutes "as it is written", from election laws to Second Amendment rights.

statements.quote: As Senate President, I stood up for Arizona families by defending state laws when others refused, like ensuring fairness in women's sports.
statements.context: From the Bio page of his campaign website.

statements.quote: I've led the charge against unconstitutional mandates, fought for our Second Amendment rights, and worked to keep government in check.
statements.context: From the Bio page of his campaign website.

record.text: As Senate President, his survey response says he has stepped in to defend Arizona laws the Attorney General's office declined to defend, including litigation at the U.S. Supreme Court.

researchNotes: Slate from Ballotpedia and FOX 10 Phoenix's voter guide (Mayes and Petersen are the only attorney general candidates listed). The Arizona Secretary of State's candidate pages returned 403 to automated requests, so the official certified list was not checked; no Libertarian or other candidate was found for this office. Petersen's statements are quoted from his own campaign website, not from Ballotpedia's quotation.
